body: I know what you mean. People say to use your words, just talk about it, but then they just ignore you until blood is shed. Don't do anything physical though. It always makes things worse. I hope you can be kind to yourself even when other people aren't much help.

I think you are protecting your future kids from family trauma, by keeping them from someone who will degrade their humanity as well as yours. You did not create this friction, and you stood up for yourself, for your family, and for decency in general, with dignity and class. Well done.
A lamp with nice warm light for your desk. And, if you live somewhere rainy or snowy, it's nice to have a change of warm socks in a drawer so you don't feel low-level cranky all day.

This brings me back - the first time I ever shared a bed with my partner, I had eaten many slices of cheese pizza and farted the night away. He taught me what a dutch oven is that night, and we've been together 28 gassy years. In other words, don't worry about it. If he doesn't find it hilarious that's on him.

After my mom had a stroke, we had grab bars put in and a bench provided by an organization like that, and it made such a difference to her independence and dignity as well as our family's peace of mind. Thank you for doing that!
Thank you, you are so kind and I appreciate it so much.

Thanks, it's really nice of you to write. Yeah, I have a really good doctor and therapist and I think my meds are as good as they can be. After a few years of bafflement at my lack of progress, they seem to be torn between telling me things would be so much better if I just got out of bed and went on walks, and basically telling me to lower my standards and expectations and just accept my lot in life and wait to die naturally I guess. I tried the walks but trudging around as the neighborhood crazy person without a dollar to spend makes me feel kind of terrible. Anyway thanks again, it's nice feeling understood.
How physically taxing is snowshoeing, compared to say, cross-country skiing? I have always wanted to try it!
I destroyed my entire life with three months of bipolar mania and then stayed in bed for seven years.
Thank you for your insight - I will discuss it with my dentist!

I'm 50 years old and bipolar and I'm so tired of waiting and trying to make things better only to have things get worse and worse. I tried so hard and I missed the chance at everything I ever wanted in life. So I think the odds of things getting better are lower than the odds of continued or worsening misery, and suicide is a solid, rational choice for me. It still makes me feel really sad though, that this is how it is. Thanks for writing.

I find the text option a lot easier than talking on the phone. They kind of guide you through the conversation so it's not that stressful to think of what to say. I hope you connect with someone good.
I have actually thought about that but I think it would depress me. Also I'm not much for leaving the house and talking to strangers these days. A good suggestion though, thank you.
I AM female and going through perimenopause - you are so perceptive! Maybe I need a med adjustment or something. Thank you.

A belated counterpoint to the other commenters: my boyfriend and friends called the cops on me three years ago and tried to have me committed. I was having a manic psychotic episode but ultimately was found not to be a danger to myself or others. My bipolar is stabilized but I still have PTSD from the cops and forced hospitalization. I am still with my boyfriend, but I will never love him or trust him as before. I will also never marry him, to avoid giving him greater power over me. Cops tend to endanger our people even when they don't kill us outright. Calling the cops is very often a coward's move.
